sourceRefs.locator: IV.22, MGH SS rer. Merov. 1.1, pp. 154–155. Chilperic uses royal treasure and enters Paris. His brothers dislodge him. The narrative pairs each of the four kings with a predecessor and a sedes.
IX.20, copy of the agreement at Andelot. Guntram retains the third part of Paris formerly held by Sigibert. Clauses on Cahors and Galswinth’s other cities.

summary.de: Sohn Chlothars I. Gregor nennt Reims als seinen Sitz bei der Teilung von 561. Im Vertrag von Andelot erscheint später sein einstiger Anspruch auf einen Teil von Paris.
summary.en: Son of Chlothar I. Gregory names Reims as his seat in the division of 561. A former claim to part of Paris subsequently appears in the treaty of Andelot.
